cards.headline: Anthropic cuts cache read costs by 75% for Claude Fable and Mythos 5.1
cards.hook: Cache reads drop to $0.25 per million, but base input/output rates stay at $10 and $50.
cards.tldr: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 with a significant pricing update. Cache reads have fallen 75% to $0.25 per million, while base input and output pricing remains unchanged at $10 and $50 per million respectively. The platform reports over 2 million monthly views, indicating sustained audience interest. This adjustment targets the cost of retrieving stored context rather than altering fundamental compute costs. For teams running high-frequency inference with context reuse, this lowers marginal costs without touching core model rates.
cards.memeLine: Base rates didn't budge, but your cache bill just got a haircut.

cards.headline: Meta’s Data Center Robots: Tugger Carts and Laundry Folds
cards.hook: Meta is putting robots to work in data centers. One folds laundry. One moves racks.
cards.tldr: Meta has been experimenting with robotics inside its data centers since at least 2023. A YouTube video from that year showed a self-driving tugger robot moving heavy server racks and a wheeled, barcode-reading robot tracking inventory. Meanwhile, Watney, launched in 2023, demoed a laundry-folding robot it claimed could also handle janitorial work. The push suggests a convergence of logistics automation and facility maintenance. Whether these demos translate to reliable, large-scale deployment remains the open question for the next phase of infrastructure scaling.
cards.memeLine: My robot doesn't fix bugs, it just folds the laundry while the servers melt down.

cards.headline: NVIDIA and Apple Unveil Compact AI Computers for Robots
cards.hook: New hardware prioritizes reliability and bandwidth over raw speed.
cards.tldr: At Computex 2026, Jensen stated that performance per watt, reliability, and long lifetime are the core features of future GPUs. This focus shifts attention from benchmark peaks to sustained operational stability. NVIDIA and AMD have published results on larger models such as DeepSeek V4 Pro and Kimi K3, using AgentX. The infrastructure supports this by ensuring that for every XPU, 1.6Tb/s of global bandwidth will travel to the global switch tray over the copper backplane. These compact units aim to deliver generational gains by solving the thermal and connectivity bottlenecks that plague current deployments.
cards.memeLine: We stopped counting FLOPS and started counting uptime.

cards.headline: MetaRoCE: The NIC Sees Intent, You See Throughput
cards.hook: Meta’s new RDMA transport scales linearly. The joke is that it finally works.
cards.tldr: Meta validated MetaRoCE across multiplane topologies with up to 4,000 concurrent connections, confirming linear throughput scaling. It consistently beats RoCEv2 on speed and latency, proving the fabric sees packets while the card sees intent.
cards.memeLine: The fabric sees packets; the NIC sees intent. I see a bill for more switches.

cards.headline: From Atari to EVE: DeepMind’s AI Just Learned 3D Games
cards.hook: It beat Lee Sedol in Go. Now it’s exploring No Man's Sky.
cards.tldr: DeepMind reveals its AI can master complex 3D environments like Valheim and Hydroneer, building on the legacy of DQN which learned 49 classic games without specific engineering. The leap from flat screens to open worlds marks a significant shift in research capabilities.
cards.memeLine: Fifteen years later, the tutorial level is an open world.
